steps.title: Subjunctive for stance: identify the trigger and the subject change
steps.body: In B2, learn the subjunctive as a meaning choice. It often follows necessity, emotion, doubt or evaluation: il faut que, il est possible que, je doute que, bien que. The subjunctive is usually needed when the trigger expresses a stance and the next clause has its own subject. After certainty or an established fact, the indicative is generally used (je sais que…). When the same person does both actions, an infinitive is often more natural (il faut vérifier). Memorize common irregular forms in useful chunks, then test the whole sentence—not just the verb ending.

steps.title: Subjunctive for stance: identify the trigger and the subject change
rows: Il faut que l'agent confirme la démarche.
The agent needs to confirm the process.
Il est possible que le délai change.
It is possible that the time limit will change.
Je doute que cette consigne soit complète.
I doubt that this instruction is complete.
Je sais que le formulaire demande une date.
I know that the form asks for a date.
It is better to verify the information.

steps.prompt: Choose the standard pattern after il est possible que.
steps.explain: Possibility expressed with il est possible que generally takes the subjunctive.

options: Bien que le formulaire demande une date.
Je doute que le formulaire demande une date.
Je sais que le formulaire demande une date.
Il est possible que le formulaire demande une date.
steps.explain: Savoir que expresses certainty and is followed by the indicative.

steps.prompt: When is an infinitive often natural?
options: When the same person performs both actions
Whenever there are two different subjects
steps.explain: With the same subject, a verb plus infinitive is often natural.
